Lina: Heads-up: brought up rk-3b-quant-primed (PTQ int8) on holdout. Weird mix: NDCG@10 up +0.018 but MRR@10 down -0.038.
Diego: That delta profile smells like top1 shuffling while tail gets slightly better. Any dataset or preprocessing changes between runs?
Lina: No intentional dataset change. Runs: run://2026-03-22/rk3b-ptq-holdout (sha: c3f9b2a1). Baseline run://2026-03-15/rk3b-fp16-holdout (sha: 7a1d4e2c).
Zoe: Did we use the same candidate pruning and anchor weighting? Small reweighting on anchors can move top1 a lot -> MRR hit.
Lina: I pulled the candidate dumps and compared ordering. There are cases where tie scores flip due to int8 quant noise around the 2nd decimal.
Diego: Can you paste a tiny example?
Lina: Sure, found a query where baseline top1 = candidate A, quant top1 = candidate B. Scores: A 0.7234 -> 0.7211, B 0.7228 -> 0.7229. So the delta is tiny.
Lina: Also noticed a small change in our sampling: the holdout split used for the new run included 4.2% more short-form queries (<= 6 tokens), which are very sensitive for MRR.
Zoe: Short queries amplify tie sensitivity. Two action items: 1) check sampling parity 2) run a deterministic tiebreaker test (stable sort by doc_id) to see if flips persist.
Diego: For quantization angle: is this PTQ only or did we apply activation rounding fudge? PTQ random seeds or calibration data difference can introduce bias.
Lina: PTQ with calibration set sample seed=42. I re-ran with seed=7 and saw slightly different top1 flips but same aggregated MRR drop.
eval-bot: job run://2026-03-22/rk3b-ptq-holdout completed. metrics: NDCG@10: 0.751 -> 0.769, MRR@10: 0.498 -> 0.460. (delta ndcg +0.018, delta mrr -0.038)
Zoe: Let's add a targeted topk-stability scan: rerank.eval --runs baseline,quant --slice topk:1 --compare-per-query. Count fraction of queries where top1 changes. That will quantify how much of the MRR loss is from top1 instability.
Lina: Running that now locally. Quick heads: top1 flip rate = 6.1%, top3 flip rate = 2.7%.
Diego: 6% is sizable. If many of those flips move to a slightly better alternative (hence NDCG up) but worse top1, that's exactly the profile.
Zoe: Could be our anchor-weight term is tuned for fp16 score distribution. Quant compresses dynamic range, so anchor_weight needs rescale. Try re-scaling anchor weight by 0.95 and re-evaluate on a 20k sample.
Lina: I'll try scaling anchor weight and also run a candidate-normalizer parity check (we had a previous bug where tracer inserted zero-width space in some candidates).
Diego: Also consider soft-tie smoothing: when score difference < 1e-3, use lexical tiebreaker or stable doc ordering to reduce churn. Add that as a non-invasive change for experiments.
Lina: Agreed. I will: 1) run sampling parity diff to ensure holdout composition identical, 2) run anchor_weight sweep [0.9,0.95,1.0,1.05], 3) run tie-stability pass with stable doc_id tiebreaker. Posting results later.
Zoe: For onboarding CI, propose: small fast check on quant candidate dumps: top1 flip rate < 2% vs fp16 or fail. Also assert samplewise NDCG not drop >0.01 for core cohorts.
Lina: Good gating rules. I'll open a PR with parity script + top1 flip check and the anchor-weight sweep notebook.
Diego: One more note: when reporting MRR/NDCG deltas in the console, include cohort breakdown by query length and by anchor presence. That will make future triage faster.
ops-bot: created ticket #ML-2754 "rk3b ptq top1 flip investigation" and linked run artifacts.
Lina: Thanks all. Quick numbers from the anchor sweep (20k sample): anchor_weight 0.9 -> MRR delta -0.012, 0.95 -> -0.006, 1.0 -> -0.038 (current), 1.05 -> -0.055. NDCG mostly increases across sweep. So 0.95 looks promising.
Zoe: Great, prioritize 0.95 test on full holdout. If full holds, we can land a small mapping layer in serving that adjusts anchor weight for quantized models.
Lina: Will run full holdout with anchor_weight=0.95 and stable tiebreaker now. Will post final metrics when done.
Diego: Nice work. These micro-adjusts for quant layouts are expected; good that we have quick sample pass to iterate.
Lina: Posting full-run soon.
